analysis_trace: Trial NCT05183763 is a randomized controlled trial comparing STAR-MAP (health coaching + reminder tools) versus MARS-MAP (reminder tools only) in adults ≥40 years with hypertension and low medication adherence (PDC<0.8). Primary endpoint: proportion achieving PDC≥0.8 at 12 months. Secondary endpoints include changes in PDC, self-reported adherence (K-Wood-MAS-4), urine metabolite adherence, BP control, and quality of life.

Evidence base: Retrieved protocol design paper (Europe PMC 42173438, May 2026) confirms trial rationale and endpoints. No outcome results available as of knowledge cutoff (trial recruiting, expected completion 2027).

Indirect evidence: Meta-analyses of health coaching and medication reminder interventions for hypertension show modest adherence improvements. Digital reminders alone typically yield small effects (absolute PDC improvement 5-10%); combined health coaching may add incremental benefit.

Evidence-role assignments: All retrieved sources are design papers or indirect systematic reviews. No direct numeric results for this trial. Evidence role: indirect_direction for adherence and BP endpoints.

Population/drug match: Adults with uncontrolled hypertension on antihypertensives. Intervention combines behavioral coaching + digital reminders vs digital reminders alone. Mechanism aligns with adherence behavior change literature.

Key uncertainties: No outcome data available; effect size estimates rely on external RCTs with varying adherence baselines and intervention intensity. BP control depends on adherence improvement magnitude.

Primary endpoint prediction: Based on adherence intervention meta-analyses, STAR-MAP likely achieves modest absolute increase in PDC≥0.8 proportion (estimated 12-18% absolute difference vs control). Predicted effect: +0.15 difference in proportion.

Secondary endpoints: Mean PDC change predicted +0.10 to +0.15; self-reported adherence (K-Wood-MAS-4) directionally improved but modest; urine metabolite adherence likely improved consistent with pharmacy PDC; BP control proportion predicted +10-15% absolute increase; SBP/DBP mean changes predicted -5 to -8 mmHg and -3 to -5 mmHg respectively; SF-12 quality of life likely modest improvement (+2 to +4 points).
Safety: Behavioral intervention; no significant safety signals anticipated. No adverse event endpoints specified in contract.
